Hi Mel, sorry you're dealing with this. I can't diagnose from a forum post and I haven't seen your leg, so take this as general info. What you're describing sounds like an overload issue in the mid-portion of the Achilles, which usually settles with the right loading rather than rest alone.

A couple of things to correct first. Stretching it hard into a burn and leaning on the wall isn't the go with a sore tendon, and a cortisone injection near the Achilles is something to avoid because it can weaken the tendon. Please don't go down that route.

Loading is the main treatment:
- Heel drops are fine, but heavy slow calf raises have better evidence behind them at the moment. Build from two legs to one as it allows.
- On bad days, isometric holds (pushing up onto your toes against a wall, 30-45 seconds each) keep the tendon working without flaring it.
- For pain, up to about 3/10 during loading is generally OK, as long as it's settled by the next morning. If it's worse than that or still sore the next day, back off the load.

Dropping the k's for a while would also help. Going from 30 to 48 in three weeks is a big jump for a tendon to keep up with.

Stop running and the calf work and get it checked that day (GP or ED) if you get a sudden pop, a kick in the back of the leg, or you can't push off on your toes. That could be a rupture.

Otherwise, if it's not settling within 3-4 weeks, see any sports physio who can assess it properly.

On a related note, some antibiotics (fluoroquinolones like ciprofloxacin, for example) are linked with tendon problems. If you're ever prescribed one and notice heel or calf pain, tell your doctor straight away.

Good luck for Rottnest.
